chapter_theme: The pure states beginning with waking (சுத்த நனவாதி): waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond are matched to the tattvas, the malas and places in the body, and each state is divided into all the others, as the soul drops its instruments and passes inward to turiya and the beyond where it becomes Siva. Among these sit verses on the malas that hide the soul (rice and husk), the one herdsman of the many cows, and knowledge that knows itself.
structure_note: The chapter opens with bindu and the states (2187, 2188), lists the tattvas (2189 to 2191) and the malas and bound soul (2192 to 2195), then maps the states onto tattvas and the subtle body (2196 to 2201). 2202 to 2206 divide each state into the others. The rest mixes the soul's rise through the states (2207, 2212, 2216 to 2218), knowledge knowing itself (2209, 2224), the malas and their cure (2210, 2211, 2213), symbolic verses on the mind (2214, 2215), yogic verses (2219 to 2223), and a close (2225, 2226).

2187.reading: The gross states beginning with waking and subtle prakriti, the twenty-five, are the power of bindu; the soul's own bindu stands and goes forth, and in this way dream mingles into waking.
2187.nuance: நனவாதி (waking and the rest) opens the chapter's subject. ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as the twenty-five lower tattvas; how bindu, the soul and the states fit together here is not clear from the verse.

2188.reading: Within waking, those in the beyond-state are like the newborn lying still, those in turiya like infants crawling, those in deep sleep like children walking and growing; when dream runs within waking, the work is done well.
2188.nuance: The verse seems to match the states within waking to a child's growth, lying, crawling, walking. The direction of the comparison, and what நன்செய்தி (good affair) means in the last line, are uncertain.

2189.reading: Close-knit ritual is the Siva tattva; with it come undivided blissful yoga, great grace and learning, the sacred form one fixes on with its many qualities, and in knowledge all that moves and stays, as far as the cosmos.
2189.nuance: The verse lists without connecting words, so how கிரியை, சுகயோகம், பேரருள் and கல்வி relate is a guess. It may describe what the pure (சுத்த) states open on to.

2190.reading: From the first, the Lord set the tattvas in place: supreme Siva, Shakti, Sadasiva, flawless Isa, pure vidya, then bodha, kala, time, niyati and mahamaya, down to the last.
2190.nuance: The list runs from the five pure tattvas (Siva, Shakti, Sadasiva, Isvara, Suddhavidya) to the impure ones begun by maya. போதம் and நீதி are not standard names in this list; நீதி ஈறாக may mean 'down to the end, in order'. என்னே may be wonder or 'what is this'.

2191.reading: Siva shining in radiance, Shakti, Sadasiva, Isa, the fiery vidya, raga, kala, time, stainless vidya, niyati, mahamaya, and the flawless purusha and the rest, with the soul at the end, make thirty-six.
2191.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the standard count of thirty-six tattvas. The order differs from 2190 and from the usual Siddhanta order, and அனல்வித்தை and மாசகல் வித்தை look like two vidyas, pure and impure; ஆன்மா ஈறு may be the soul at the end of the list or the atma tattvas.

2192.reading: Anava, maya and karma are the malas; as bran and husk cover the sprouting grain, the soul stands as the rice, unlike Sthanu who has none: cherish it by separating your bonds.
2192.nuance: The rice image is a classic of Siddhanta: the husk and bran are with the grain from the start, as the malas are with the soul, yet are not the grain and can be removed. தாணுவை ஒவ்வாமல் sets the bound soul apart from Siva, who is free of them.

2193.reading: The cows are of many colours but their milk is of one colour, and the herdsman who grazes them is one; if the herdsman lays down his staff, the cows will not let go of their master.
2193.nuance: பசு means both cattle and the bound soul, so the verse is read of souls, many in form and one in nature, and of the one Lord who tends them. கோல் போடில் may mean laying the staff aside or striking with it; traditionally it is the Lord's act of grace, after which the souls cling to him.

2194.reading: Body, senses, mind, bright intellect, chitta, the mighty ego and ignorance remaining, that soul perishes; and if its delusion branches further, it reaches the seven hells.
2194.nuance: The list is the soul's instruments, ending in அறியாமை, which here stands for the mala of ignorance. மயல் (delusion) that grows is what leads down; the verse does not say the instruments themselves are bad.

2195.reading: The beyond-state that does not know itself is anava; turiya, where words are known, is karma; deep sleep that follows is the desire spoken of; and the rest, of food, is dream and waking.
2195.nuance: The verse seems to match the states to the malas: atita to anava, turiya to காமியம் (karma), sushupti to desire, and dream and waking to the grosser bonds. உண்டி (food) in the last line is obscure; the matching is the tradition's reading.

2196.reading: In waking there is no dream; in the five of waking, the subtle without dream is seen as deep sleep; prakriti that eats fire, and maya that gathers itself; in waking, turiya and atita come to the fore.
2196.nuance: Each line is compressed and the syntax uncertain. தனலுண் பகுதி (prakriti that eats fire) is obscure and may be corrupt.

2197.reading: When twenty-five of the thirty-six withdraw, there is waking in waking; when six more leave, waking in dream; when the other five also go, at the end of waking is deep sleep; in this, there is maya alone.
2197.nuance: The counts follow the tradition that each state is marked by fewer tattvas in play. The arithmetic and which tattvas are meant are not stated, and the states named may be read differently.

2198.reading: The purusha who came in maya, in turiya, leaving the order that arose and becoming not even that, goes far off with the kevala seed; then the body that was taken has no use.
2198.nuance: சேயதே வலவித்துடன் is obscure; read as கேவல வித்து, the seed of the kevala state, it fits the next chapter's subject, but the reading is a guess.

2199.reading: The soul is the knower in atita and turiya; if it practises atita-turiya by that, the one who rose in atita and became knowledge is completed in turiya, in the ripe fire.
2199.nuance: மானன் and முதிய அனல் (ripe fire) are obscure. The verse seems to say the soul, as knower, matures through the higher states.

2200.reading: Waking has twenty-five with ten; dream, with the twenty-five at hand, is in the throat, they say; the three who saw falsehood, with purusha, are deep sleep; the one who saw the truth, settled in the navel, is two.
2200.nuance: This is a variant of 2142: the states descend through places in the body (brow, throat, heart, navel) with fewer instruments in each. சுழுனையின் may be சுழுத்தி (deep sleep) or சுழுமுனை (the central channel). The counts differ from 2142.

2201.reading: Union with the eightfold subtle body is waking; three in it is dream; two in it is deep sleep; entering one in it is turiya.
2201.nuance: புரியட்டகம் is the subtle body of eight (the five subtle elements with mind, intellect and ego, as tradition counts it). The numbers mark how much of it stays active in each state.

2202.reading: Waking in waking is the ordinary run of things, like flowing water; dream in waking is remembering and forgetting; deep sleep in waking is not searching within; turiya in waking is Nandi in the beyond.
2202.nuance: From here to 2206 each state is divided into the states within it. புனலில் வழக்கம் may mean the habitual flow of life or of the waters of the body; the reading is uncertain.

2203.reading: Seeing in dream as if awake is waking in dream; seeing in dream and forgetting is dream in dream; seeing not-seeing is deep sleep in dream; and turiya comes in inferring and the like.
2203.nuance: அனுமாதி (inference and the other means of knowing) attached to turiya is unexpected; the line may be corrupt or mean that judging what was dreamt is the highest level within dream.

2204.reading: Waking in deep sleep is the appearing that nothing appears; dream in deep sleep is its truth in deep sleep; deep sleep in deep sleep is knowledge destroyed by knowledge; turiya in deep sleep is a void beyond words.
2204.nuance: பாழ் (void, waste) is a term Tirumular uses for states beyond form. The lines read as pointers rather than definitions.

2205.reading: Waking in turiya is the awareness that knows what is good; dream in turiya is the awareness that knows the inner; deep sleep in turiya is the void; turiya in turiya appears itself as the supreme.
2205.nuance: இதம் may be 'the good' or 'this, the present'. வியோமம் (space, void) is a technical term for the pure expanse. தோன்றிடும் is printed கோன்றிடும்.

2206.reading: Knowledge knowing knowledge is waking; knowledge reaching unknowing is dream; that unknowing of knowledge is deep sleep; knowledge becoming knowledge of knowledge is turiya.
2206.nuance: The verse plays on அறிவு and அறியாமை in every line, so the sense rests on wordplay. It reads as the four states seen as states of the soul's knowing.

2207.reading: He who is everywhere, having left the five malas, with knowledge as his form, after delighting in it, leaves even the way of being everywhere and rises above, beyond the subtle and its hues.
2207.nuance: ஐம்மலம் (five malas) extends the usual three. Whether தான் is the freed soul or the Lord is unclear; read here of the soul whose pervasiveness was hidden by the malas.

2208.reading: Twenty-five, six and five more are in waking, aimed at as waking, dream and deep sleep; body, then the subtle, true prakriti, maya and doubt: he is one in that turiya.
2208.nuance: The counts echo 2197. அவன் அத்துரியத்தன் may say that the soul beyond these is in turiya, or that the Lord is; the verse does not settle it.

2209.reading: All this time he did not know what this is; after knowing it he knew nothing else; after knowing the knowledge that knows 'this is it', he is one whose nature is to know it.
2209.nuance: ஈதென்று (as 'this') opens every line. The verse moves from first person (அறிந்திலேன்) to third (இயல்புடையோனே), which may be the speaker describing himself or the knower in general. Knowing it ends other knowing: the knower becomes what knows.

2210.reading: As life of life, with form and without, as union with others, as knowledge and as fullness, the loving Shakti and the Lord are the world and all; without them, all is the delusion of darkness.
2210.nuance: இருண்மூடம் (dark delusion) is read as the soul's state under anava without the Lord's presence. இயற்பின்றி may mean 'without their nature' or 'without their working'.

2211.reading: Making the soul good through the power in raga, the Lord fashioned the fitting bonds, the five malas and the thirty-six distinctions of tattva, and set the instruments, so that the malas may be cut.
2211.nuance: The second half states a Siddhanta teaching: bodies and instruments are given not as further bondage but so that, working through them, the soul can be rid of mala. The first line, சத்தி இராகத்தில், is obscure.

2212.reading: In waking-atita anava is in its own truth; when waking-atita reaches turiya, and anava does not leave in waking-atita, the truth of the Supreme abides in waking-atita.
2212.nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் opens every line. Tradition distinguishes the atita of the bound soul, a blank under anava, from the atita of the freed, the Supreme's presence. The third line (ஆணவம் தான்விடா) seems to contradict this reading and may be meant as 'when anava has gone'.

2213.reading: By the mixing of mala, Shakti was hidden, knowledge was hidden, Sthanu was hidden; when the mixing of mala ends, there is the light of the moon.
2213.nuance: மலக்கலப்பு (mixture with mala) opens three lines, each naming something hidden. மதியொளி is the moon's light, or the light of understanding; both readings stand.

2214.reading: In the bewildered mind are three lions, in the mocking heart four fox cubs, in the dividing heart five elephant calves, and to the hostile heart the milk is two.
2214.nuance: The animals are symbolic and the verse does not gloss them. Commonly the three lions are taken as the three malas, the four foxes as the four inner instruments, and the five elephant calves as the five senses. பாலிரண்டு (milk, or share, of two) is obscure.

2215.reading: Before the mind, scattering and rising as the eighteen roaring eyes leave, is shaken, if you stand in the true way, there will be an elephant coming with a roar.
2215.nuance: பதினெட்டுக் கண்கள் (eighteen eyes) is unexplained; it may be a count of faculties or of sects. ஆனையும் ஆமே can mean that one becomes like a charging elephant in strength, or that the elephant (the senses or mind) is won; both readings stand.

2216.reading: In waking, twenty fall away; in dream, with the inner instruments; standing at the front, he shook them off and entered within, and without thought stood in deep sleep.
2216.nuance: நாலைந்து (four fives) is the twenty, presumably tattvas. முனவகம் is obscure and may be corrupt. The verse describes the soul passing inward through the states as it drops its instruments.

2217.reading: He who stood so, the teacher, being in turiya, united, taking on the world's rules of discipline, went to the turiya-atita and staying there a while became the Supreme, the stainless one.
2217.nuance: ஆசான் may be the soul as master of itself or the guru; நியமாதி is the yogic niyama and the limbs after it. சிலகாலம் (a while) suggests a stage rather than an end.

2218.reading: That Isa, as vidya in the atita, swallows the world; leaving Sadasiva, the great Shakti and the five forms, he becomes Siva, reaches silence, and is the light of the root.
2218.nuance: The verse may describe the soul rising through the pure tattvas (vidya, Isvara, Sadasiva, Shakti) to Siva. உலகுஉண்டு (having eaten the world) and மூலத்தன் are read here as absorbing the world and being at the source.

2219.reading: Those who have seen within the three regions the good lord of the realm of maya, and pass on contemplating him inwardly, open out; on the lotus, the one above is below, and the cosmos itself is within.
2219.nuance: மண்டலம் மூன்று are traditionally the regions of fire, sun and moon in the body. The syntax of the second and third lines is uncertain.

2220.reading: The flock of birds cried, not knowing the time; women stood confused, not knowing; our Lord stood so that none could know him; those who know the secret wear him on their crown.
2220.nuance: The birds and women may stand for the senses and their objects, or be plain images of not-knowing. வேதுஅறியா may be வேதம் அறியா (the Vedas not knowing). சூது (secret, subtlety) and உச்சி (crown) may point to the crown of the head in yoga.

2221.reading: Knowing the intent, I saw the nine regions fit together there; seeking the Lord of the worlds I knew the great Lord of the gods truly, knew him in his fullness, and stood with mind fixed.
2221.nuance: ஒன்பது கண்டம் may be the nine parts of the earth or nine places in the body. The verse is a first-person testimony, its repeated அறிந்தேன் building to the mind standing still.

2222.reading: As he who kindles the lamp's flame, the lamp's flame is the root practice; in the place of the root, by the rule there, that lamp burns, taking the other, the moon region.
2222.nuance: மூல சாதனம் and மூலத்தானம் point to the muladhara. The lamp lit at the root and fed from the moon region above is traditionally read as the fire of kundalini meeting the moon's nectar; that reading is the tradition's.

2223.reading: If you ask about the open space where the skull of the five who seek inward is gathered, he said: look upward, and at the junction where the five meet the eye's glass sees; that is the intent.
2223.nuance: The five (ஐவர்) are probably the senses drawn inward. அண்ணாந்து பார்த்து (looking up) and the சந்தி (junction) are read as the gaze to the point between or above the brows. கண்நாடி may be the eye as a mirror or a seeking eye.

2224.reading: The knower knows what is not known; one who does not know is not the knower of himself; who can know the knower who knows without knowing, joining the unknowing state to the knower?
2224.nuance: Built on அறி in every phrase, like 2206 and 2209. அறியாதவத்தை may be அறியாத அவத்தை (the unknowing state) or அறியாத தவத்தை. The last line ends in a question that tradition reads as the knower known only by being it.

2225.reading: We have told the vision of turiya: the void, the rare faults, the Brahmin and the rest; beyond great time is turiya, and the rare atita is in the atita itself.
2225.nuance: தூடணம் (faults) and அந்தணவாதி are obscure here; the line may be corrupt. The verse reads as a closing summary of the turiya teaching.

2226.reading: The sentient one in maya is bound to prakriti; removing that other part of maya is itself maya; it becomes kevala; in the womb of sakala maya, the jiva of men immersed there is in turiya.
2226.nuance: கேவலம் and சகலம், the soul's isolated and embodied states, lead into the next chapter (கேவல சகல சுத்தம்). The syntax is uncertain and the last line may mean that even immersed souls have a turiya.

links.note: A near-repetition: both place waking, dream, deep sleep and turiya at the brow, throat, heart and navel with fewer instruments in each. They differ in the counts (ஐஐந்தில் against பன்னான்கில்) and in the third line (பொய்கண்ட மூவர் against பொய்கண்டிலாத புருடன்), which may show a corrupt copy in one or both.
Both use பசு in its double sense of cattle and bound soul. 2015 sorts the cows by what they yield, only the mature ones giving milk; 2193 makes them all one in their milk and one in their herdsman.
2192 names the three malas and calls for separating the soul from them; 2211 says the Lord gave the tattvas and instruments for exactly that, so that the malas might be cut.

Both make release the end of an obscuring mixture: the Kural's stainless sight, freed from confusion, removes darkness and brings joy; Tirumular says Shakti, knowledge and Siva are hidden by mala and light appears when the mixture ends. Tirumular names what hides; the Kural names only confusion.
Both trace a bad end to delusion: the Kural's confusion that takes the unreal as real yields a joyless birth, and in 2194 the soul whose delusion grows reaches the seven hells.

The Kural guards the five senses with the elephant goad of firmness; Tirumular ends his verse on standing in the true way before the mind scatters with a charging elephant. The pairing holds if 2215's elephant is the mastered senses or mind; if it is the strength one gains, the images only touch.
2209 says that after knowing the knowledge that knows, one becomes that knower; 2224 turns this into a riddle: who can know the knower who knows without knowing?

source_issues: 2205 line 4: கோன்றிடும் is a misprint for தோன்றிடும்.

2200 is a variant of 2142 with different counts (ஐஐந்தில் for பன்னான்கில், ஐஐந்து பத்துடன் for ஐஐந்து மத்திமை) and a different third line (பொய்கண்ட மூவர் புருடன் சுழுனையின் against பொய்கண் டிலாத புருடன்இத யம் சுழுனை); one or both may be corrupt.
Obscure words that may be corrupt: 2196 தனலுண் பகுதி, 2198 சேயதே வலவித்துடன் (perhaps கேவல வித்துடன்), 2216 முனவகத்தே, 2225 அரியன தூடணம் அந்தண வாதி.
